Honestly, one of the best meta roleplaying games I've played; and this perfectly filled my Mettaton-shaped hole in my heart, if you know what I mean.

Although it may seem like a funny dating simulator on the surface, this game rang the same bells with me as Undertale did way back then. Beautiful hand-drawn anime art style, banger soundtrack (that jazz track in Darling's bedroom, oh my God!), unique twist on its genre with the premise (dating goddesses of eldritch/Lovecraftian horror), adequately delivered horror elements, charmful characters and meta game mechanics that really kicked me in the balls when I tried to 100% the game and made feel really bad for my actions (the game knows what actions you take and goes smirky about it, like Undertale).

The game really did an Undertale-style knockback at me when [spoiler]I tried out the breakup spell in an alternate timeline after completing the romantic kissing ending in Chapter 1 and in Chapter 2, Ln'eta knew what atrocity I did to her in another world; like how Flowey knows how the player manipulates the game world[/spoiler].

Sucker for Love is a very impressive roleplaying game on its own with lots to love about it, but fans of Undertale would appreciate the game the most. It's like one those anime games Alphys would play to geek herself out.

This is the perfect game to get your meta RPG fix if you did not like Deltarune as much.

My only complaint about the game is that I played through the endings I was interested in 3 hours. That's very short, this should have been an 8+-hour-long game.

Besides that, this is a 9/10 masterpiece that dating sim and meta RPG fans, especially of the Undertale and Doki-Doki Literature Club variety, would likely regard as a modern classic.

Very cute (yet terrifying) visual novel with nice interactive elements. As the description suggests, you romance Eldritch gods, three of them to be exact. Each of them has their own book with various rituals to perform in order to win their affections, but the focus of each book is a little different. The first one is straightforward, simply following the instructions. The second involves "acting out a play" which requires paying attention to the stage directions and reciting the lines properly. The third is more time sensitive, needing to find the relevant page in the book based on what's happening and carrying out the ritual in time.

There are three chapters, with two true endings in the first and last chapters, and 6 in the 2nd chapter. The checkpoint system makes it not too difficult to get each ending, but at the same time the game itself is extremely short (I got 100% in under 3 hours). At $10, this length would normally make me not recommend a game but... honestly, it's just so cute and charming I still enjoyed it. Each girl has a distinct personality, and even though you might not like them all, it's still entertaining [spoiler]L'neta best girl though[/spoiler]. You also might learn something about Elder Gods from the game while you're at it!

If you like monster girls, definitely a must buy, especially if you can pick it up on sale. However, if game length is important to you, you might want to wait for a steep discount.

Super good all the way through and especially creative in the last chapter, an awesome twist on a visual novel that combines both my favorite things in the genre: horror and romance. Great writing, voice acting, and the art is especially wonderful in both style and technical execution. Really can't wait to see what else the devs put out!

The only complaint I can come up with is that I ran into a few bugs, but they were hardly experience-ruining. For instance, the window randomly being too large to read the bottom text (fixed by exiting and re-entering fullscreen with alt-enter), the character sometimes disappearing when they aren't supposed to (usually fixed by leaving the room and coming back). Really minor stuff, hardly worth pointing out.

If I had any suggestions, a history feature also would have been nice since I accidentally skipped dialogue a couple times, but that's just my own user error.

The length of the game is in a nice sweet spot, not too long or too short. I noticed Steam only recorded me with 2.3 hours in the game, but it just didn't detect me playing when I started it for the first time. I think it took me around 6 or 7 hours total to finish all the endings?

As for cost, it's totally worth it at full price. In fact I honestly think $10 is a steal. I have a lot more gushing I would like to do, but it would be better if instead of reading this, you were just playing the game. So... you should go do that.

Sucker for Love: First Date is honestly one of my favorite Visual Novels. I was honestly a little skeptical on playing this one, but I was blown away by the quality and value this provides.

The start to the game really sets the whole tone with the anime-like music and an art style that grasps the player instantly. I was instantly drawn in as hearing the music and hearing the voices for the first character you meet. Yup. Voices! And they are actually wicked well done! The voice actors really seemed like they enjoyed reading their parts and are perfect for who they played.

I really enjoyed how this novel had multiple branches in decisions and endings. Without spoiling too much, you can interchange certain items and it changes how the novel is played out. The novel has a puzzle-like aspect to it and I think that really adds to the whole directive the devs were going with here. Obviously, I had to try and find all the endings and, did I mention secrets?? The final *final* ending was actually pretty tricky. It took me a while to get the hang of it, but definitely worthwhile!

I really, REALLY enjoyed this visual novel. I hope to see more from these devs in the future because I intend to fully endorse anything they put out. Overall, I fully recommend.

I had Sucker for Love on my radar for a little bit, having seen it first as part of a Dread X collection that I can't for the life of me recall the name of right now. Regardless, the game immediately caught my eye, because spooky visual novels are usually pretty great.

And I have not been disappointed, the game is pretty masterful at keeping a tone that can balance between creepy, funny and even emotional at times. The four characters (counting the protagonist) are all really fun and memorable, and the fact that I can't say who my favorite is says a lot about how good they all are.

Gameplay-wise, it's actually quite fun, and uses its mechanic (the spell chanting) in very creative ways, especially in the final secret chapter. The checkpoint system also allows for hunting endings pretty conveniently, and it thankfully never gets too tedious. My only gripe may be with the second chapter, as its endings can be very confusing and hard to unlock.

Otherwise, Sucker for Love is a very cute visual novel with some nice spooky elements, though I wouldn't call it an outright horror game. Definitely worth your while if you're looking for something funny and well-written to get through in a night.

Sucker for Love, or SFL as I will likely call it the rest of this review, is a fantastically written monster dating sim. While the runtime is short for an initial play through, there are branching endings and paths that make replaying a worthwhile option. Each of the three chapters have multiple endings, with chapter 2 in particular having 6 possible outcomes for the story! This was a really fun game to play on Twitch, my viewers had a great time seeing each chapter come to a close and I had a blast being a down bad goober for a few hours.

SFL was a pleasant surprise for me, and it was just the right amount of a subversion of the dating sim genre to get me interested. I'm not usually one to dabble in these types of games but the writing and the surprise gameplay mechanics that presented themselves made this a game worth checking out. I will very likely play and check out the sequel as well, SFL did a fantastic job at setting up plot lines that can be explored in sequel titles.

Pros:

* Great writing, each girl has their own quirks and personality. D, the player character, likewise has differing attitudes and responses to each girl.
* The three chapter setup offers each girl multiple endings, making replays worth it to see everything.
* Chapter 3 specifically throws in a new gameplay loop that offers a fun subversion to the dating sim genre.
* Story felt tight and concise, giving the player enough to be satisfied with what was offered while leaving enough open for sequels.

Cons:

* Short runtime may be a turn off for some players, game only takes about 3 hours to complete if you only intend to play each story once.
* Controls in some chapters are a tad sluggish. Feels like you are fighting the controls to complete your objective.

[h1][b] TLDR: A short and funny visual novel that despite the name and theme, manages to be tasteful and deliver a good message. [/b] [/h1]
[h1]PROS: [/h1]
+Solving ritualistic puzzles can lead to some humorous moments, especially when you deviate from the main path. 
+Some witty and cute narrative moments.
+Unique occult setting.

[h1]CONS: [/h1]
-Controls are primitive.
-No achievements.
-Some stereotypical anime tropes.

[h1][b] Gameplay (Controls/Mechanics/Loop/Difficulty) – [7/10] [/b] [/h1]
As typical with most visual novels, the vast majority of Sucker for Love (SfL) is simply reading through the story. The part that is different from other VNs becomes the ritualistic puzzles you need to solve for the story. I thought it was a nice change of pace using various items like a knife, robe, candles, lights, and chalk symbols in a very specific manner to solve the puzzles. 
The controls were a bit primitive. You cannot even use WASD or arrow keys to move back and forth in your room. Otherwise, normal KB & M controls. 
The difficulty I found pretty easy for all but the final storyline where you have some fairly ambiguous puzzles thrown at you and no explanation for failure. Still, these can be brute forced. 

[h1] [b] Graphics (Quality/Art style/Animations/UI) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
Typical anime-style graphics. There is no animations, just new drawings of the characters. Overall, pretty simplistic, probably able to run easily on a PS3. 

[h1] [b] Audio (Sound Effects/Score/Voice Acting/Ambient) – [5/10] [/b] [/h1]
I found the musical score to be largely forgettable. The voice acting is decent enough, though your character isn’t voiced despite having no customization or choices. 

[h1] [b] Content (Game world/Narrative/Lore) – [6/10] [/b] [/h1]
I found the world too simplistic, as there are literally only 3 zones, but perhaps that’s a given for such a short game. 
The story is also simplistic where [spoiler] your character pretty much summons a demon and dooms all of humanity for a smooch. [/spoiler] Still, SfL isn’t really trying to be profound, it’s just goofy fun. 

[h1] [b] Replay Factor (Side quests/NG+/Player Choice) – [2/10] [/b] [/h1]
There is no NG+ to partake, nor achievements, so this really tanks the replay value. There are branching storylines, [spoiler] but each leads to an ending where you most likely die, so it creates an illusion of choice. [/spoiler] With only one real path, the game will take you about 2-3 hours to complete. 

[h1] [b] Final Verdict – [6/10] [/b] [/h1]
Overall, I enjoyed my time with Sucker for Love. The unique puzzle aspects were something I wish was built out more in a longer visual novel. 

[h1] [b] Recommend? [Y/N] [/b] [/h1]
[h1]Yes [/h1]
But only if it’s on a deep sale. It’s such a short game with no replay value or branching paths that I wouldn’t pay for a few dollars for it.

First of all, I’m actually too much of a chicken to play the secret ending or secret route part myself because well, I was creeped out enough by the other two chapters…

Another thing: DDLC was compared to this game in some reviews I saw and I want to kind of disagree with that comparison. To me DDLC had totally different vibes than this game and I actually found DDLC a lot creepier.

Basically, this is a short novel with horror elements and some jump scares (for me at least). There are at least three romanceable options: Ln’eta and Estir and in the secret route Nyanlathotep. Your character works as a host and has a weird obsession regarding eldritch gods. Long story short, the character manages to summon one and makes a deal with the summoned Ln’eta. He has to perform various rituals to increase her affection and, if he succeeds, she will reward him with a [strike]kiss[/strike], I mean “smooch”. Seems easy enough, right? Well, just play the game and see for yourself…

Let’s talk a bit about the characters and the corresponding routes. 
Ln’eta is the protagonist of the first and of the second chapter. The first chapter is meant to be an introduction to the whole gameplay and setting: The novel feature of this game is that you need to hover your mouse over the words that are written in your Necronomicon to “speak” them and perform the corresponding ritual. Additionally, you will realize fairly quickly that this novel has indeed horror elements to it.

Estir is one of the protagonists of the second chapter. The second chapter is actually a bit different than the first chapter. While in the first chapter you have a pretty much straightforward story line, where you do not have any choices and are basically only performing the rituals, the second chapter has multiple endings and choices. Additionally, there is a “penalty” for performing rituals wrongly. 

The third chapter is about Nyenlathotep and its focus are timed rituals. Basically, the first two chapters “prepare” you for the “boss battle” so to say. However, like I said, I did not play it myself, but watched a Let’s Play. It actually takes multiple trials to win there and it’s kind of both creepy and challenging.

To summarize, I enjoyed playing (and watching) this game a lot. The idea that you “chant” spells by hovering with your mouse over them and you “fail” them, if you move your mouse too quickly, is cool and novel for a visual novel. Additionally, the story line and the characters were very interesting and enjoyable, so I had fun playing this game. I’d recommend it to everyone, who has a few hours to spare, enjoys a funnily written original story (with horror elements) that you shouldn’t take very seriously and wants to challenge themselves a bit.

I wanted to write a more comprehensive review than those I've seen promoted on this page, as those are your usual one-line memes.

Slight gameplay spoilers, obviously. Don't read if you want to go in blind, but I personally wanted a bit of an explanation of what the game was like before I bought it.

So, this is really quite a clever little dating sim, which has you enacting rituals to smooch the various cosmic horrors. The gameplay is your typical VN fare, shifting items in and out of your inventory and progressing through dialogue, but you also have a grimoire that has you read incantations to progress along the routes, which is a nice touch and I really like how you have to slowly drag your mouse across each incantation for you to cast it, you can't go too fast or else it doesn't work. There's only one location, the apartment itself, and the items don't really change between routes. You're also told what you're missing if you cast an incantation without everything set up properly, which is very helpful and appreciated.

The writing is very fun and lovingly parodies both dating sims and cosmic horror. There's some surprisingly tender moments, mostly with Ln'eta (the Cthulhu-girl). The art is fantastic, too, very 90s anime, which is one of my personal favorite styles.

The third act is a twist on the formula of the first two acts, and is very fun and engaging. I love how it played out, but I won't spoil that here.

I think my only critique is I kept running into glitches and little bugs. Moving to different routes to get all the endings was a bit wonky, as some flags and triggers didn't match up quite right, and there's one instance where I flat out couldn't select a particular bookmark, despite having it unlocked. I also had a bookmark unlocked that I technically shouldn't have at that point in the game. There's some weirdness in selecting items covered by other ones, and you can't switch routes if you have your grimoire up. These can all be ironed out, though, and didn't detract from my experience.

One other thing I wanted to mention: there's an instance of (implied) animal abuse in Act 1. I don't recall that being listed in the trigger warnings at the beginning of the game, but worthy of note nonetheless.

All in all, I quite liked this despite an initial negative reaction upon first seeing it, and am definitely interested in seeing the sequels!

Sucker For Love: First Date is something of an enhanced version of the original Sucker For Love made for the Dread X Collection 2 (which I've also reviewed in the past). Seeing as that was a highlight of that collection, I thought it worthwhile to play the expanded version of that initial game, and wanted to give my two cents on it. So, here we are.

Sucker For Love: First Date plays as something of a point and click visual novel. You sit in the shoes of our protagonist, D (yes, that's his name), a man with a single minded goal: To smooch Eldritch beings. To do this, he gains access to a Necronomicon-esc tome that, while not looking like one, is actually a cult ritual book to summon Ln'eta, a waifu-ifed version of the great Cthulhu! In order to earn the smooch, D must complete various rituals, which the player does by flipping through the book, collecting the required items via a simple point and click interface, and then chant the rituals by dragging the mouse over the appropriate incantations slowly. It's certainly a unique mechanic for a dating sim.

However, the game features a checkpoint system with a flowchart, and multiple different endings, both good and bad. This allows the you to see what would happen if D did something in a ritual wrong, or some other thing that causes him to die or go insane (I mean, we are talking about smooching Lovecraftian beings, so what's a little sanity for the promise of smooches?).

Upon completing a date with Ln'eta, you unlock a second episode of sorts, where you can date Ln'eta again, OR you can choose to go after her eternal rival, Estir, a girl modelled after the King in Yellow themself, Hastur the Unspeakable. If you choose to go down Estir's path, the rituals shift into a recreation of the play "The King in Yellow," inspired by the story of the same name's use of said play, which is one of the primary sources of Hastur's lore. But Estir is offering TWO smooches for finishing it, so heck yeah we gotta do it! It's otherwise the same mechanically as the stuff with Ln'eta. Of course, you CAN try to go for both, but it likely won't end well for you.

However, that's not all. If you manage to fulfil some special conditions in your pursuit of smooches, you can unlock the third episode, featuring Nyanlathotep, a waifu version of the Crawling Chaos, Nyarlathotep. However, in her case, you aren't in it for smooches this time. Instead, ol' Auntie Nyan Nyan (she likes this nickname for some reason) wants you to suffer for trying to consort with her nieces, or just going after the unspeakable horrors for smooches in general. This is a survival gauntlet, where you have to use the book to survive an onslaught of small rituals that, should you fail, will end you. It's a tense final challenge. In the end though, you give the ol'Clawing Chaos something to fear when she sleeps: D and his need for endless Eldritch Smooches!

The game is quite funny, especially if you're a fan of both a massive weeb (which I very much am) and a fan of Lovecraft and associates works within the Cthulhu Mythos. There's tons of little jokes that fans of those things will get more out of than the average player, but I assume if you're interested in this game, you're a Lovecraft loving weeb like me, so you'll probably get a kick out of it. The writing is generally really good, and it's clear Akabaka has more than a basic knowledge of Lovecraftian Horror fiction, since, as previously stated, it has a lot of nods to the lore of the creatures that he waifu-ified.

The game also has solid voice acting all around for the three lovely ladies you meet along the way. There are ONLY 3 voices, as D lacks a voice, but that's usually expected in these types of games. There is technically a voice reciting the unholy forbidden spells you use, but it's just a basic sound effect. The sound design outside of that is pretty basic. It does have a fun little anime ending theme inspired song in it, so that's pretty neat. The art direction is also really solid, capturing both cute and horror really well! I don't really have much to say beyond that in terms of anything beyond the writing though, given how short it is.

It's not without it's issues though. There are a few instances of visual glitches, usually with how the text is displayed. I think there are one or two voice lines that also just may not play, which is a little sad, but it's not a total deal breaker. I didn't come across any game breaking bugs or anything, so it's really just a tiny bit of grime on an otherwise solid experience. I do think the price may come off as a touch steep for some, given that it's quite short, clocking in at a little under 3 and half hours for me, and I was aiming to 100% it. There's also a few missing quality of life features for these types of games, like being able to see a log of what characters said. The game is simple enough that a save system isn't really needed, especially with the checkpoints you get, but I'm mentioning that purely because some people want that in a dating sim/visual novel type game.

Overall, I'm gonna give Sucker For Love, First Date a solid 4/5. I think I gave the Dread X Collection 2 original a higher score, but that was within the context of a greater collection of bite-sized games. As a stand alone title, I think it's better than the version from the collection, as it has more content, but I am left wanting more. At time of writing, the long awaited sequel, Sucker For Love: A Date To Die For, has just come out, and I did just finish it, so I'm going to be reviewing that game too.

An amazing subversion of the visual novel format. The 90s anime artstyle is beautifully executed with its saturated colours and bright appealing character designs. The story balances 3 different love interests without compromising the stories or character of any of them, easter eggs and hidden details being incorporated into the gameplay to add to the mystery of discovering the unknowable. The game balances humour and horror stunningly well, with humour cutting the tension of the more eldritch elements, while the horror creates immersion and adds stakes, grounding in how it re-emerges to add paranoia to the lighthearted nature of the dating sim. It reminds me of Doki Doki literature club in it's subversion of the genre, but it manages to supercede it as the story is able to balance the weight of the horror throughout the story, instead of revealing it as an endpoint. It carries all of it's best elements and improves upon it, having more of what was so compelling to begin with, and having a final battle within the visual novel setup that manages to have real stakes and horror, working with the gameplay elements to make for an eldritch final girl moment. Amazing game, I reccomend it to everyone, I look forward to seeing more content from the franchise as they build from an incredibly strong foundation, with amazing characters and compelling worldbuilding and story.

Our lives and freedom is an illusion, or rather a big joke. We are not the beloved children of an universal God, but the slaves and playthings of Elders Gods ready to end our reality just by awaken from their slammer.

Not in this reality thankfully. In this one an obsessed person wants to smooth a Rule 34 Cthulhu named Ln' eta by following the instructions of a pink survival guide, for starters. He is 100% focused on completing all the rituals and ready to doom his reality...what.

Just because it is a parody visual novel of the Lovecraft's mythos and Anime of the 90s, doesn't mean that the horror theme of the game takes a back seat entirely. It is a successful mix of comedy and horror together.

More specifically all the dialogues you hear from the talented voice actors that give life to our sexy elde-, I mean young Goddesses can be both hilarious and terrifying based on how you will please them.

In the rituals you also need to perform, you won't be safe either. You need to do a lot of sacrifices to complete them with the first one your own sanity (to be fair you are clearly already insane if you want to kiss a sexy octopus).

The next in line evolve your body. In all seriousness if you hate body horror and gore, you better avoid the game. But yeah, the rituals affect your body in many gruesome ways.

Did I mention even if it is a visual novel at heart, the rituals are in a way your 'dialogues options'? Yes, this reminds me a lot of some other games which follow this kind of trend and I am in love with it.

Interesting concept, decent execution. With all the complexity of doing eldritch rituals, I expected the progression to be less linear.

The mechanics are hit and miss. There were pretty frequent visual bugs with equipping items, especially in chapter 2. Perhaps the game engine wasn't being used as intended, or perhaps the dev team was inexperienced or rushed. Good job to whoever did the art though.

I turned the voices off since they didn't add much, and while the dialogue was pretty clever most of the time, the game and story just didn't have much depth. I don't know how much getting voice actors cut into the budget, but my guess is the game could have been more fleshed out story-wise by not including it.

The price point is also a bit high for how short the game is. It took me like 3 hours including the secret final boss fight, which is easily manageable if you read through the book a few times before starting it (kinda tedious; ending wasn't particularly rewarding either). Almost every ending felt rather abrupt and unsatisfying.

Overall, this game just feels like a big missed opportunity that could have been much more. It tries to do cutesy romance, cool spellcasting, and eldritch horror, but nothing stands out as 'great'. It's all just 'there'.

- There's no "Are You Sure?" when you hit "close game". My hands move faster than my head, sometimes, and I closed the game that many times when I just wanted to go to the checkpoint menu.

FURTHER PRAISE
- It's cute and funny. If it weren't for this bug, I could see how so many people are enjoying it and recommending it to others.

I played the Dread X Collection and was waiting patiently for this and was glad it came out! I think the art is amazing, the voice acting is great, and the puzzles/bigger story is fun. Character designs are camp and fantastic. 

You're going to notice though that I don't recommend this game. 

It's buggy in some ways when it comes to getting endings, so you may end up like me replaying for one of the endings (the top one in Chapter 2) and being unable to get it even though you did the right thing a few times. That was frustrating and I hope it's fixed soon.

Additionally, my biggest problem is the final chapter. I didn't mind having to find secrets to get it, and I didn't mind that it was short if you didn't do the "fight," but what I did mind is how a game that was a slow paced but dark, multiending "dating sim" turned in to a quick paced mess that went on for way, way too long. 

Final "boss" fight spoilers: [spoiler]The fact that I had to do some of the spells multiple upon multiple times, plus sometimes I got hurt and didn't understand what was even happening. There was a lot going on there, and while I enjoyed the idea of it, the bugs that occurred (the guy who is coming in the door, i literally closed the door 30 times before i just gave up and let him eat my turtle each time, RIP) and the length it went on made it crippling hard and unpleasant. I wish there were like 10 puzzles and you'd have to do like 7-8 or even 9 of them, but in some of my attempts I had to do some of them multiple times, and some of them were overlapping each other and hurting me while I attempted to complete one of them. I gave up when I realized I had made it through 10 different ones, died, and didn't even know how many more there would be.[/spoiler]

I'm not sure if many of the reviewers got to this part in the game, as it requires completion of secrets to get there, but I felt unhappy and stressed out by the end of it, I tried over and over to beat it but eventually realized that it just wasn't fun so I gave up. 

Over all, if you have money to spend and like the aesthetic, feel free to grab it, but otherwise, I wouldn't spend the money again if I knew the final area was like this and I'd end up this frustrated with it.
